stem: At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?

choices.text: Decline because four prior refills exhaust the federal limit if its alternate trigger can be documented.
Dispense indefinitely until the prescriber cancels it.
Require a new prescription because every controlled-drug fill is nonrefillable.
Allow two more refills because the six-month window has two months left.
One additional refill may be lawful because neither the five-refill cap nor six-month clock is exhausted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'One additional refill may be lawful because neither the five-refill cap nor six-month clock is exhausted.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Decline because four prior refills exhaust the federal limit.' would require that the numerical ceiling were four rather than five. The decisive cue appears in 'At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Decline because four prior refills exhaust the federal limit.' would apply only if the numerical ceiling were four rather than five; 'At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Dispense indefinitely until the prescriber cancels it.' would apply only if Schedule IV prescriptions had neither a count nor time ceiling; 'At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Require a new prescription because every controlled-drug fill is nonrefillable.' would apply only if eszopiclone were Schedule II; 'At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Allow two more refills because the six-month window has two months left.' would apply only if time remaining could increase the five-refill maximum; 'At same-day pickup, a Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills with one refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'One additional refill may be lawful because neither the five-refill cap nor six-month clock is exhausted.': supported by schedule iii-iv refills.

related_facts: eszopiclone (Lunesta) is used for treatment of insomnia; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
